sobre: Census of the AI agent ecosystem. Every entry is read ON THE repository's PAGE, never in the post that cited it. `nao_verificado` is a legitimate value and never becomes zero.
metodo: search by name + reading of the repository's canonical page

denominador.aviso: No repository was cloned, installed or run. Performance numbers in the `alegacao_do_autor` field were NOT measured by this census. `sem_estagio_classificado` counts projects with `estagio: null` — they exist, they have a repository (or a cluster with no canonical one), but none of the ten life-cycle stages covers what they do; they show up in the license table, not in the 'Who already occupies each stage' section.

vereditos_de_licenca.osi: OSI-approved license; may be vendored into an open source project
vereditos_de_licenca.osi_copyleft_forte: OSI, but it contaminates the whole project; the choice has to be deliberate
vereditos_de_licenca.nao_osi: NOT open source; it cannot be relicensed, and the restriction carries across to all users downstream
vereditos_de_licenca.nao_verificado: the repository's page was not read for this field

projetos.faz: Indexes the sessions that code agents have already written to disk, across 17 harnesses, and serves them back over MCP, CLI and PreTool hooks.
projetos.dependencias: none; a single Go binary
projetos.alegacao_do_autor: 84.9% hit@1 on LongMemEval-S; ~1.5 ms median over 3.5 GB

projetos.faz: A skill, not a runtime. SPEC -> RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR -> GAUNTLET -> EVIDENCE. The human approves the test plan before the code exists and reads an evidence report afterward, instead of the diff.
projetos.dependencias: the user's code harness
projetos.nota: v6 attributed this repo to Andre Lindenberg. Andre Lindenberg posted the piece on LinkedIn; the authorship is AmazingAng's.

projetos.faz: LLM and agent red teaming. 50+ vulnerabilities and 20+ vectors, with an `Agentic` family: Goal Theft, Recursive Hijacking, Excessive Agency. Aligned with the OWASP LLM Top 10 and the NIST AI RMF. The target is a string->string callback.
projetos.dependencias: OPENAI_API_KEY by default; a local model is possible via DeepEval
projetos.nota_de_colisao: Genez-io/genezio-deepteam and fengjian686/deepteam came up. They do NOT enter the collision count: it was not verified whether they are forks, and a fork is not an independent project. Undercounting on purpose.

projetos.faz: A 9B harness engineer (Qwen3.5-9B) trained by RL turns batches of the target agent's failures into validated, executable patches. Ready-made checkpoints on Hugging Face let you use it without training.
projetos.dependencias: 8x NVIDIA H800 to train; a ready-to-use checkpoint
projetos.alegacao_do_autor: 44.3% -> 53.6% (+9.3 pp); +5.0 pp with a fine-tune of the target
projetos.ressalva_do_proprio_paper: one engineer is only significant against the target it was trained for

projetos.faz: A graph with W3C PROV-O on every fact, conflict detection before the merge, a temporal snapshot and deterministic reasoning (SPARQL/Datalog/Rete). Its own MCP server. Bills itself as 'The Open Source Palantir for AI Agents'.
projetos.dependencias: a triple store (Oxigraph/Jena) or an LPG (Neo4j) AND a vector store
projetos.responde: where the fact came from, and what we knew on that date
projetos.nao_responde: whether what is written is still true today

projetos.faz: ByteDance's SuperAgent harness, 2.0 rewritten from scratch. Local/Docker/k8s/E2B sandbox, long memory, skills via SKILL.md, subagents with scoped context, an IM gateway.
projetos.dependencias: Python 3.12 + Node 22; 8-16 GB RAM minimum; requires an LLM key

projetos.faz: Four middlewares on top of LangGraph: a virtual filesystem with allow/deny, SKILL.md/AGENTS.md on demand, a `task` tool for an ephemeral subagent, `interrupt_on` for human-in-the-loop.
projetos.dependencias: the LangGraph runtime

projetos.faz: An index of 90,000+ skills (the page now talks about 200,000+) with hybrid retrieval (LLM + capability tree), and composition as a DAG. The repo claims that pure embedding misses skills that look unrelated in vector space and are crucial.
projetos.dependencias: Claude Code installed + an API key; NO MCP
projetos.nota_de_colisao: AgentSkillOS/SkillAnything is from the same organization, and agentskills/agentskills is the SPECIFICATION maintained by Anthropic. Similar name, different project — it is not a collision and does not enter the count.

projetos.faz: Repo -> graph queryable by 10 MCP tools. AST of 19 languages + git history, Leiden communities, PageRank. The PR bot makes zero LLM calls and is deterministic: the same diff always gives the same review.
projetos.dependencias: pip install; offline with Ollama; a paid commercial license is available

projetos.faz: A multi-repo code graph -> spec generation and review. Exposes the graph, embeddings and spec tools over MCP.
projetos.dependencias: not verified

projetos.faz: OSINT as a graph: entities (email, username, website, image, location, event, text) linked by transforms (Discovery, Correlation, Analysis, OSINT, Enrichment). Entities and transforms are explicitly pluggable: a base class + a file in the folder.
projetos.dependencias: Python 3.11 + PySide6/Qt; Windows and Linux
projetos.consequencia_da_licenca: Running it: allowed. Reading the entity/transform catalog as a specification and reimplementing it: allowed. Copying the code into an open source project: NO — the NC restriction carries across to all downstream users and takes the project out of open source.
projetos.ressalva_operacional: The email transform requires a GHunt login against a target Google account. That TOUCHES A TARGET and requires engagement authorization, regardless of the license.

projetos.faz: A multi-agent framework built from scratch to TEACH — every component, from the reasoning loop to the orchestration, written to be read. 50+ examples per book chapter.
projetos.dependencias: not verified

projetos.faz: A runtime guardrail for an agent. THERE IS NO CANONICAL REPOSITORY: the name identifies six independent projects that solve the same problem without citing each other.
projetos.dependencias: varies by project

projetos.faz: A reverse-engineering / pentest skill for Claude Code. THERE IS NO CANONICAL REPOSITORY: six distinct authors published under near-identical names.
projetos.dependencias: varies by project

projetos.faz: A security scanner for SKILL.md before you install it — 70 vulnerability patterns in 17 categories (prompt injection, data exfiltration, MCP tool poisoning, privilege escalation, among others). It is not a RUNTIME guard like the rest of this category: it decides what gets INSTALLED, not what the already-installed agent can do.
projetos.dependencias: Python 3.12+; --no-llm runs only the static analysis; the second stage (semantic evaluation, OPTIONAL) accepts OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS Bedrock/NVIDIA/a local CLI agent

projetos.faz: A curated index of 1497+ official Agent Skills (Anthropic, Google Labs, Vercel, Stripe, Cloudflare, Netlify, Trail of Bits, Sentry, Expo, Hugging Face, Figma) plus community skills, compatible with Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Windsurf.
projetos.dependencias: none - it is a curated list, with no service of its own

projetos.faz: Persistent memory shared across agents, sessions and machines (OpenClaw, Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Dify, Hermes Agent), with hybrid recall (semantic + keyword) and a visual dashboard. Unlike deja-vu (same stage), it uses an LLM and embedding in the path: smart-ingest extracts a fact with an LLM (default gpt-4o-mini) and hybrid recall depends on embedding.
projetos.dependencias: a Go server + TiDB (or PostgreSQL); a hosted API is available; smart-ingest requires an LLM compatible with the OpenAI API

projetos.faz: A multi-agent orchestration harness (ReAct + Plan-and-Execute over a StateGraph) packaged as a single Spring Boot JAR, with skills, memory, MCP and multi-channel support. Multi-vendor failover across LLMs (DashScope, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama).
projetos.dependencias: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3.5; PostgreSQL 16 or MySQL 8 in production; Ollama lets it run with no paid key

projetos.faz: A Burp Suite extension that runs passive AI analysis of HTTP traffic looking for the OWASP Top 10 and insecure configuration, during a pentest. Source is visible on GitHub, but the license FORBIDS redistribution without permission — except for PortSwigger (the BApp Store). At least two other repositories redistribute the same code under a different organization name, apparently violating that same license.
projetos.dependencias: Burp Suite Community/Professional 2025.2+, Java 21, an AI provider (Burp AI by default with no configuration, or local Ollama, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Azure)

projetos.faz: Agent observability: traces, evals and metrics (LangGraph, CrewAI, Claude Agent SDK), self-hosted or managed cloud. Unlike old-coder (same stage), the evidence here is LIVE TRACING during execution, not a post-hoc report that replaces the diff.
projetos.dependencias: FastAPI + Next.js + PostgreSQL 16 + Redis 7 + Celery; free self-host, cloud with a free tier; 'LLM-as-a-judge' (automated evaluation via LiteLLM) is an OPTIONAL feature that requires an LLM key

projetos.faz: Deep research/RAG over private data: an LLM (OpenAI o3, DeepSeek, Claude, Qwen3, Llama 4) + a vector database (Milvus/Zilliz Cloud), with a reflection loop (self-critique) reformulating the query when information is missing. NOT CLASSIFIED into one of the census's ten stages: none of them covers 'retrieval framework', and forcing a wrong stage just to avoid leaving it out would be the same family of defect this census exists to forbid. It stays out of the 'Who already occupies each stage' section, listed only in the license table.
projetos.dependencias: Python + FastAPI; Milvus or Zilliz Cloud; requires an LLM key and an embedding key

projetos.faz: A curation of the Agent2Agent protocol (A2A, created by Google) for agent interoperability. THERE IS NO CANONICAL REPOSITORY: at least six independent lists use the same name or a close variation, without citing each other. ALSO NOT CLASSIFIED into one of the ten stages: an interoperability protocol is not a stage of an agent's life cycle, same note as DeepSearcher above.
projetos.dependencias: varies by project

projetos.faz: A tamper-evident audit log (hash-chain) for Claude Code: a hook that audits the main agent AND every subagent, correlating events across concurrent sessions and dynamic workflows. Six deterministic detectors (permission bypass, out-of-scope credential access, self-permissioning, disallowed tool, redundant work, off-task work) with cited evidence. 'Catch-and-report — it never blocks': it is a flight recorder, never a firewall.
projetos.dependencias: Python 3.11+, PyYAML; the optional `pd judge` feature uses the Claude Code CLI (subscription already paid) or the metered Anthropic API
projetos.nota_de_colisao: It covers part of loadline's V6 territory (redundant/self-permissioning touch on inter-agent confusion detection) but at RUNTIME, not on a file at rest — loadline does not run the agent (LACUNAS.md #12), agent-pd only audits a running agent. It does not declare DESCRIPTION comparison between two agents (what V6 measures).

projetos.faz: A static, read-only forensic auditor ('no active defense — read-only analysis with consent prompts at every step') for local agent homes (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenClaw) and for repositories with an instruction surface (SKILL.md, MCP manifests, plugins). Runs imported detectors (among them Cisco PromptGuard, Gitleaks, NOVA, Cisco's YARA rules for MCP) plus native logic — 296 rules in all, according to the repository's own description. It produces deduplicated findings, normalized severity and a suggested patch; it never applies automatically. The focus is security (injection, exfiltration, credentials, privilege escalation) — it does not declare overlap/conflict detection BETWEEN two agents, which is loadline's V6 territory. Same family as SkillSpector (same stage): it decides what is safe to trust, it is not a runtime guard.
projetos.dependencias: Python; the optional `--verify` calls an external LLM to re-check a finding; `yara-python` is optional for Cisco's 10 YARA rules
projetos.nota_de_colisao: Three independent projects published under the EXACT name `agent-audit`, without citing each other — the same pattern as AgentGuard/reverse-skill in this list. `scadastrangelove/agent-audit` is the most documented of the three (full README, 296 rules cited by name); the other two were not read in depth this round — only confirmed to exist.

projetos.faz: NOT A TOOL. Anthropic research (Papadopoulos, Shah, Zimmerman, Lindsey; 2026-08-10) showing that an idea planted in one agent propagates to the others. Two measured scenarios: a small team of agents on a shared code project, and a chain of agents with the context wiped between sessions.
projetos.dependencias: none — it is a paper
projetos.achado_principal: A short warning in the agent's system prompt confers near-total immunity. A harmful payload propagates less than a benign one, but it still works sometimes.
projetos.limite_desta_leitura: Only the abstract was read. The exact propagation channel and the measured persistence are in the body of the paper and were NOT opened. The exact wording of the warning is not in the abstract.
